newsitem.title: USA: Dun & Bradstreet to gain from purchasing.
newsitem.headline: Dun & Bradstreet to gain from purchasing.

text.p: Dun & Bradstreet Corp has "revolutionized" its purchasing department and expects to add three cents per share to its bottom line this year as a result, Chairman Volney Taylor said on Tuesday.
"This year, our purchasing department expects to add three cents to earnings per share," Taylor told a meeting of the National Association of Purchasing Management.

Speaking to Reuters after his speech, Taylor said that the company is shooting for a roughly seven percent increase in earnings this year. In the first quarter ended March 31, earnings totalled 22 cents per share, up from 18 cents a share a year earlier, on an adjusted basis.

Taylor told the purchasing managers that they had to change the ways they carry out their business to make do in an increasingly competitive and deregulated world economy where inflation is low and it is difficult to raise prices.
"Purchasing agents won't survive this revolution," he told the group. "To survive it ... let alone exploit it ... you've got to be an agent of change."
That means focusing more on the bottom line, trying to anticipate change rather than react to it, and approaching purchasing as a way to manage suppliers, he said.
